facts.text: The Truth in Lending Act applies to loans made to consumers.
A closed-end loan is a credit card.
If an institution solicits customers to open credit card accounts, it must determine the customer's credit rating.
Prepaid finance charges include fees that are also known as the APR fees.
Prepaid finance charges are paid by the borrower after loan closing.
For loans secured by a dwelling, if the APR may increase during the life of the loan, the institution must disclose the maximum rate that may be imposed during the loan term.
The Truth in Lending Act requires disclosure of finance charges, payment schedule, and total of payments, except total maximum late fees that can be assessed.
The Truth in Lending Act ensures that loan terms are disclosed in a meaningful way.
